title: LKAB deploys 120-tonne electric trucks underground
summary: Swedish mining company LKAB is deploying two 120-tonne battery-electric Scania trucks at its Malmberget iron ore mine. Operating at depths of up to 1,250 metres, the vehicles have already transported more than 100,000 tonnes of iron ore since entering service.

title: Waymo puts Zeekr-built Ojai robotaxis into regular service
summary: Waymo is using its new generation of robotaxis for paid rides for the first time. The Zeekr-built electric vans are initially operating in San Francisco, Los Angeles and Phoenix, equipped with Waymo’s sixth-generation autonomous driving system.

title: Renault 5 gains more range and new entry-level LFP version

A new entry-level version with an LFP battery is also joining the line-up, although it will not be available in Germany for the time being.

title: Octillion adds 3 GWh of battery capacity in India
summary: Octillion Power Systems has opened its third battery factory in India. The new plant in Gujarat has an annual capacity of more than 3 GWh and will supply battery systems for electric cars, commercial vehicles and buses.

title: Xpeng posts €2.5 billion in revenue in Q2 2026
summary: Chinese EV manufacturer Xpeng generated revenue of 19.74 billion yuan (approximately €2.5 billion) in the second quarter of 2026. Growth was driven primarily by its development partnership with Volkswagen. Xpeng also raised $900 million for its robotics subsidiary Dogotix.

title: Mexico unveils Olinia Carga electric light truck

Most recently, he was responsible for the company’s smaller models, including the EX30, EX40 and XC40. His predecessor, Anders Bell, will now lead a new startup initiative within Volvo Cars.

summary: In Skellefteå, Sweden, energy provider Skellefteå Kraft is testing how a pink sauna can be powered by electricity from electric vehicle batteries. The unusual project showcases the potential of bidirectional charging.

title: CityFreighter unveils electric motorhome based on Evolve platform
summary: CityFreighter, Vöhringer and Motive Development have unveiled an electric motorhome at the 2026 Caravan Salon in Düsseldorf. The demonstrator is based on CityFreighter’s new Evolve electric low-floor platform, which features a skateboard architecture.

summary: Walmart now operates EV fast chargers at 100 of its stores across 20 US states. Most locations have eight to 16 charging points with up to 400 kW, fitted with both CCS and NACS connectors.

title: E-quipment highlight: 4,400 hp Wabtec FLXDrive electric locomotive
summary: After nearly a year of operation on a dedicated track line at the Jimblebar iron ore mine in Australia, BHP is proving that these 4,400 hp battery-electric powered heavy-haul locomotives are ready for prime time.

summary: Tesla says it will officially inaugurate its new Semi factory in Nevada next month, marking the grand opening of the plant it has designed to build 50,000 electric trucks a year. summary: Tesla has lost another senior chip engineer to DensityAI, the AI hardware startup built out of its own former Dojo team. summary: Geely is developing a new 1,000-volt architecture for electric cars to further reduce charging times. The Chinese group has already installed charging points with peak outputs of up to 1,500 kW. Its latest charging tests show just how quickly its current models can recharge.

summary: A year ago, Chinese vacuum cleaner manufacturer Dreame Technology announced plans to enter the luxury electric vehicle market. summary: Texas Instruments (TI) has introduced the TMCS2100-Q1 , a coreless Hall-effect current sensor for hybrid and electric vehicle traction inverters that measures the magnetic field around a conductor in both the horizontal and vertical directions rather than on a single axis. This precision improves the torque control loop in the EV powertrain, according to TI, maximizing efficiency and power delivery across varying load and thermal conditions. DTE Energy will be among the utilities using Lansing-built cells in future storage projects. summary: Blink Charging has launched a new energy management system (EMS) designed to maximize charging capacity with existing electrical infrastructure while providing greater visibility and control over how energy is used at charging sites. title: XCharge NA powers electric aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicle at Dallas airport
summary: XCharge North America (XCharge NA), which supplies high-power EV charging and battery-integrated systems tailored to the North American electrical grid, has provided charging infrastructure for a public safety initiative at Dallas Love Field Airport (DAL). Dallas Fire-Rescue (DFR) has selected XCharge NA to deploy its ultra-fast C7 charging unit to power the airport’s Rosenbauer Panther 6×6 Electric, a fully electric aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicle. The C7AM unit delivers 400 kW of output through liquid-cooled cables, engineered to support the long-duration, high-speed charging cycles the Panther requires. “Transitioning frontline emergency response vehicles to electric significantly mitigates the logistical and environmental hazards inherent to liquid fuel on tarmacs, and

title: Nano One and Standard Lithium collaborate to qualify lithium carbonate for LFP cathodes
summary: Canada-based Nano One Materials , a process technology company specializing in lithium-ion battery cathode active materials (CAM), has produced LFP CAM and in-house battery test cells using battery-quality lithium carbonate supplied by Standard Lithium from the pilot plant at its South West Arkansas Project. Nano One processed the lithium carbonate through its One-Pot process to produce LFP CAM and then tested battery coin cells assembled in-house at its facility in Burnaby, British Columbia. The test material attained the target chemical and physical parameters, while also achieving the intended particle morphology, the company said. title: TapFin selects ELECTRA AI to power battery intelligence
summary: B2B software company ELECTRA AI, which bills itself as the “AI Brain for Batteries” platform, and Iron Horse Acquisition II have announced that India-based AI battery data intelligence platform TapFin has selected EVE-Ai Battery Fleet Analytics to strengthen its battery-level intelligence. TapFin aims to turn telemetry, battery health and utilization data into actionable intelligence across the asset lifecycle for lenders, OEMs, operators and sustainability ecosystem players. EVE-Ai Battery Fleet Analytics adds a research-grade battery-science layer, providing continuous State of Health (SoH) and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) analytics, fault detection and operational guidance. ELECTRA AI’s platform enables battery systems to be monitored, optimized and controlled across their full lifecycle

Traditional joining methods like crimping or bolting often lead to increased resistance, reduced reliability, and higher scrap rates over time. This presentation shows how ultrasonic metal welding provides a future-proof alternative for wire-to-terminal and busbar applications – delivering stronger joints, superior conductivity, and faster, more consistent production. summary: Why has Orange EV thrived while other commercial EV startups dropped like fruit flies? title: This is what the VW ID. Tiguan looks like
summary: The VW ID.4 is expected to be renamed the ID. Tiguan after its facelift. The new name is considered confirmed. And the exterior design has also been leaked ahead of the world premiere – even in moving images: A well-known auto YouTuber has sneaked a peek of VW’s hope-bearer in a short video – partially wrapped, but with clearly visible features.

title: Vehicle to life: When the Kia EV5 becomes a camping battery
summary: An electric SUV, a small caravan, and a journey to the Polish Baltic coast: The Kia EV5 had to prove itself to us not just as a tow vehicle. Thanks to 'vehicle-to-load', its 81.4-kWh battery also became a mobile power source at the campsite. And, surprisingly, the consumption with a trailer turned out to be a pleasant surprise.

summary: Tesla is subject to the largest recall campaign in China's history: Due to potential issues with the mechanical emergency door unlocking system, Tesla and other manufacturers must rectify several million vehicles. European authorities remain hesitant so far.

summary: Ubitricity and Deftpower are expanding their collaboration on smart charging in the Netherlands. At 1,500 public charging points, charging processes are to be deliberately shifted to times of lower grid load using the open OCPI 2.2.1 standard.

title: Terra Charge plans 2,500 NACS charging points in Japan
summary: Terra Charge plans to widely introduce the NACS charging standard in Japan starting in 2028. By 2033, a total of 2,500 charging points are expected nationwide. In addition to fast chargers, the operator will also focus on NACS solutions for AC charging for the first time.

title: EKPO and Akkodis integrate novel fuel cell stack into 40-tonne hydrogen truck
summary: German company EKPO Fuel Cell and Akkodis, a Swiss specialist in digital engineering, will soon integrate and test a fuel cell stack from EKPO in a hydrogen truck that achieves a system output of up to 360 kW in the demonstration vehicle. The partners plan to use the data collected for developing future fuel cell systems that can also be applied to other sectors, such as stationary energy supply, shipping, or off-highway machinery.

title: Cadillac hesitates with electric cars in the UK
summary: General Motors is reconsidering its plan to relaunch Cadillac in the UK, citing uncertainty in a "rapidly evolving" marketplace. Competition from European and Chinese brands poses potential headwinds for the US company.

title: India: Chennai flags off 130 electric buses
summary: Chennai, the capital of the southern Indian state Tamil Nadu, has welcomed 130 new electric buses for public transport services. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay flagged off the new fleet of zero-emission buses.

title: Hyundai Group integrates smart charging control from Kaluza
summary: The Hyundai Motor Group has tasked energy platform Kaluza with natively integrating smart charging controls into the Kia app and Hyundai's digital platforms. This will allow EV drivers to charge when power is cheapest and eventually participate in grid stabilising and storage with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities. The partnership will initially launch in the UK and subsequently expand to Australia and other countries.

title: Estonia plans 5 MW charger for new battery-electric ferry
summary: High-performance charging infrastructure is to be installed for electric ferries operating on one of Estonia's most important ferry routes. PSW Power & Automation is supplying its Megawatt Charging System with up to five MW of charging power. A new electric ferry is set to serve the route starting at the end of 2028.

title: AEM unveils new electric motor for heavy-duty commercial vehicles
summary: British startup Advanced Electric Machines (AEM), which specialises in electric motors without rare earth materials, will unveil the 3D model of its largest and highest-torque motor at the upcoming IAA Transportation in Germany. The new electric motor set to be available as a sample for heavy-duty applications next year.

title: JLR delays electric Defender launch to the early 2030s
summary: British automaker JLR is reportedly delaying the launch of an all-electric version its 'Defender' SUV. British media reports that although the off-road-capable vehicle had originally been slated for a new generation in 2028/29, this has now been put off until the early 2030s—and only this new generation will support electric drivetrains.

title: Lyten to acquire insolvent battery cell manufacturer Morrow Batteries
summary: US battery developer Lyten is now seeking to acquire the insolvent Norwegian battery cell manufacturer Morrow Batteries, after acquiring Swedish battery maker Northvolt. If the deal goes through, Morrow's battery technology activities could continue to be based at the company's site in Arendal.

title: ChargePoint and Cariqa partner on QR code payments
summary: Berlin-based startup Cariqa, which offers a direct payment solution for charging electric vehicles, is partnering with U.S. charging infrastructure provider ChargePoint. As a result, charging station operators can now process QR code-based ad hoc payments via the Cariqa platform.

title: Solaris to build 20 electric buses for Olomouc in the Czech Republic
summary: Solaris has signed a contract with the public transport operator in the Czech city of Olomouc for 20 electric buses. Delivery is scheduled for 2028, with an option to double the order.

title: Asahi Kasei opens new facility for wet-process battery separators
summary: Japanese chemical company Asahi Kasei has opened a new coating line for Hipore wet-process battery separators in Charlotte, North Carolina, USA. The facility marks the first step in establishing a regional supply structure for wet-process plants.

title: Hyundai invests in product offensive with first EREV models

summary: The bZ5 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y and much more high-tech than Toyota vehicles we are used to.

title: Aptera solar EV makes up to 4.75 kWh a day, independent test shows

TÜV Rheinland, the 150-year-old German testing and certification firm, ran three days of on-site solar measurements at Aptera’s Carlsbad, California headquarters and confirmed the car generated 4.23 to 4.75 kWh per day, enough for roughly 42 to 47 miles of driving on sunlight alone.

And, if you tilted your head just so, that humming might have sounded like a warning.

title: How Tesla’s solar business works in 2026 after killing Solar Roof

Now, with electricity rates climbing across the US, Tesla is trying to revive it around a new in-house solar panel and Powerwall 3 — while quietly retiring the product it was once best known for. Earlier this month, Tesla discontinued its Solar Roof , the glass solar tile it launched in 2016. It was always a tiny piece of the business, and its end says more about where Tesla solar is going than where it’s been.

title: Tesla denies rumors it’s abandoning ‘Full Self-Driving’ push in China
summary: Tesla is denying rumors that it has pulled its “Full Self-Driving” team out of China, saying its Shanghai data center is “operating normally” and that it has even reported the claims to police. title: Emobi and OmniTrust partner to advance Plug & Charge adoption

title: Asahi Kasei’s pre-doping technology cuts first-cycle capacity loss in silicon-rich cells
summary: Asahi Kasei has developed a lithium pre-doping technology for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries with silicon-based anodes. Lithium carbonate, added to the cathode as an extra lithium source, makes up part of the capacity that silicon-rich cells lose permanently during their first charge and discharge cycle. EVs are among the applications calling for higher cell energy density, according to Asahi Kasei. Development work has focused on two changes: partially replacing the anode’s graphite with silicon-based materials; and raising the operating voltage of the cathode. The pre-doping technology addresses the penalty that comes with the first. Silicon holds more lithium per gram than graphite, which is why cell makers blend it into predominantly graphite anodes. title: Generational finds cell-voltage imbalance in one in 85 used EVs tested in the UK
summary: Generational, a UK-based EV battery diagnostics company, has published an analysis of cell-level data from approximately 10,000 used-EV battery tests run through hundreds of dealers across the UK. The median vehicle showed 8 mV between its highest and lowest cell voltages, but around one in 85 tests showed an imbalance above 50 mV, and around one in 200 exceeded 100 mV. An imbalance above 50 mV requires investigation, the company says, and at 100 mV it indicates a potential underlying fault. An EV pack is built from several hundred cells connected in series groups. It stops charging when the first cell fills and stops discharging when the first cell empties, so one weak cell limits the whole battery, and a pack-level average won’t show it, Generational explains. title: Indian bus operator Fresh Bus adds 400 electric buses to ChargeZone’s charging network

Now ChargeZone has expanded its existing partnership with intercity bus operator Fresh Bus. The latter plans to add 400 electric buses to ChargeZone’s charging network, in addition to the 100 Fresh Bus buses already served by ChargeZone. The expanded operations will connect 20 cities and cover 17 additional towns across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana over the next 15 months. title: VW’s €20,000 electric car likely to be named ID. Up
summary: Volkswagen's planned electric small car for 2027, with a base price of around €20,000, will be called ID. Up and not ID.1 – according to a Spanish media report. The publication writes that VW has already finalised the model's name as ID. Up.

title: UK order books are open for Chery’s first all-electric SUV
summary: Lepas has confirmed full UK specifications for the new L6 EV, the Chery brand’s first all-electric SUV. The L6 EV offers up to 279 miles of range. Order books are due to open early in the fourth quarter of 2026. UK customers can choose between two trim levels.

title: Nickel exposure at CATL plant in Hungary
summary: The occupational safety authority in CATL's battery plant in Debrecen, Hungary, has temporarily suspended work in three areas when nine employees were found to have experienced elevated nickel exposure. The incident affects CATL amid the already delayed ramp-up of its cell production.

title: Hubject advances Plug&Charge in Japan in collaboration with Plugo
summary: The roaming specialist Hubject is advancing Plug&Charge initiative with a cooperation in Japan. There, the Berlin-based company is joining forces with Plugo, a charging infrastructure company that wants to implement Plug&Charge in the Japanese market.

title: Study highlights potential solutions to economic barriers in battery recycling
summary: Recycling EV batteries is currently not economically viable in Europe even thought it is technically well advanced. A study conducted as part of the EU project called Safeloop estimates the current loss at around 1.90 euros per kilogram of battery pack. Researchers estimate this could be rectified with different approaches – particularly in business models and more efficient processes.

title: BYD reports 10,000 Flash Chargers installed in China
summary: In spring, BYD unveiled the second generation of its Flash Charger and announced the goal of installing 20,000 of these stations by the end of this year. The T-shaped charging stations each feature two charging cables and 1,500 kW of charging power. BYD now reports having reached half of this target.

summary: Mahle has opened a production facility for electric compressors in Coimbatore, India. At full capacity, more than 300,000 units are expected to be produced there annually. The components play a particularly important role in the thermal management of electric vehicles.

title: hofer powertrain builds a battery module with programmable cell pressure control
summary: hofer powertrain has built a battery module that varies the mechanical preload on each cell in operation, a value normally fixed by the module’s physical design. The module uses a freely programmable force map that lets the pressure on the cells change with the operating condition instead of staying constant. That turns a fixed mechanical design parameter into one the battery system can actively control. title: Tesla confirms Full Self-Driving was active in a crash that killed a mother of five

title: Tracking the fatal Tesla Autopilot and FSD crashes hidden in its data

title: A second Tesla driver died stopped on a freeway with Autopilot/Self-Driving on

title: ROHM releases automotive-grade 650 V IGBTs for EV compressors and heaters
summary: ROHM has released its 4th-generation 650 V IGBTs, automotive-grade switching devices aimed at EV electric compressors and high-voltage heaters of the PTC and coolant types as well as inverters for industrial equipment. The parts carry a typical collector-emitter saturation voltage, VCE(sat), of 1.55 V and a short-circuit withstand time of 7 µs at Tj = 25° C, and ROHM says they meet the AEC-Q101 automotive reliability standard. Conduction loss in an IGBT tracks its saturation voltage, so a lower VCE(sat) means less power dissipated while the device conducts and less heat to remove. ROHM redesigned the device structure, including the process and edge termination, to raise current density while cutting both conduction and switching losses. title: I rode Juiced’s 70 MPH Nomadix electric dirt bike, and the $2,495 price is a steal
summary: The electric dirt bike/e-moto market has developed a pretty obvious split over the last few years. On one end, there’s a seemingly endless supply of inexpensive no-name machines with questionable components and varying levels of quality. On the other, there are legitimately impressive machines from established brands, but they tend to come with prices to match. The new Juiced Nomadix R lands somewhere much more interesting in the middle, offering better quality components but at a price that competes well with the budget offerings. After spending several hours riding one off-road, I think Juiced may have just created one of the best performance-per-dollar electric dirt bikes on the market. more…
